What this crew builds and repairs

Pavers are the center of the work here. That means paver driveways, paver patios and walkways and pool deck pavers, including travertine. Next to new installs, the crew does the upkeep that keeps a paver surface looking right: paver cleaning and sealing and paver restoration, which covers deep cleaning, stripping a failed sealer, releveling sunken spots, swapping cracked units and re-filling the joints.

Poured work comes after that: concrete driveways, patios, stamped concrete, slabs and repair and resurfacing. The crew also lays artificial turf and builds segmental retaining walls. Around Kissimmee the most common paver questions are about sealing in Kissimmee and restoring tired pavers in Kissimmee; in town and in the northern suburbs they come up as paver restoration in Orlando.

Paver sealing and restoration: when a surface needs which

Sealing is for pavers that are sound but dull, stained or losing sand from the joints. The surface gets washed, the joints get re-filled and a sealer goes on. Restoration is for pavers that have moved: a dip where the base settled, a corner that rocks, a puddle that never drains. Sealer can't fix any of that, because the problem sits under the surface.

On timing, the industry guide doesn't give a number of years. ICPI's Tech Spec 5 says sealers need re-coating after a period of wear and weather, and acrylics generally last a few years (ICPI Tech Spec 5). So we look at the surface rather than a calendar: water that no longer beads, joint sand washed out after a summer of storms, or color that has faded unevenly. That same guide notes that a whitish bloom called efflorescence can appear within about 60 days of an install and doesn't hurt the pavement's structure, so a fresh patio with a white haze isn't automatically a defect.

What changes when you build in Central Florida

The ground under a Clermont driveway and the ground under a Kissimmee driveway are not the same. Lake County's ridge towns sit on Candler and Astatula sand, drained so well that the water table lies below 80 inches (NRCS, Candler series). Through Orlando, Kissimmee and St. Cloud the common series are Myakka, Smyrna and Pomona, where water can stand within a foot and a half of the surface part of the year (NRCS, Myakka series). ICPI's driveway spec starts at 6 inches of compacted aggregate on well-drained ground and adds 2 to 4 inches where the soil stays wet (ICPI Tech Spec 2), so two paver bases a few miles apart can legitimately differ by a third.

Rain and heat set the calendar. Orlando International averages 51.45 inches a year, most of it from late May to mid-October (NOAA 1991–2020 normals), which is why rainy-season concrete work starts at sunrise. Orange County also appears on the Florida Senate's list of eleven counties holding most sinkhole claims (Florida Senate Interim Report 2011-104); a sunken paver field is far more often a washed-out base than a geological event, and this guide to settlement explains how to tell the difference.

Permits: who handles what in Osceola, Orange and the rest

The apron where a driveway meets the street is public right-of-way, and nearly every office here wants a permit for it. Beyond the apron the answers split. The City of Kissimmee runs driveway permits through the engineering division's online system, while Osceola County caps a residential driveway at 24 feet wide unless a conditional use is approved. Unincorporated Orange County treats residential pavers as a zoning permit rather than a building permit.

HOA and architectural review in this region

Many neighborhoods here answer to an architectural board before the city ever sees the plan. Baldwin Park's review committee meets twice a month and takes at most 25 applications per meeting; its guidelines hold a front driveway to the width of the garage door (Baldwin Park Network, ROA/ARC; Baldwin Park Residential Guidelines, 2024). Lake Nona's Laureate Park wants its board's sign-off on any improvement, sent by email ahead of time (Laureate Park HOA FAQ), and Celebration's committee works from a monthly posted deadline (Celebration, Architectural Review Committee). Florida law now stops an association from demanding a building permit before it reviews your request (F.S. 720.3035). The step-by-step version is in this HOA approval guide.

How an estimate works

You call (689) 354-0025 or send the form with your address and a few photos. We schedule a visit, measure, check the slope, the soil and where the water goes, and note the HOA or permit questions. The written scope that follows lists base depth, paver type and pattern, joints, sealer, permits and cleanup, so two bids can be compared line by line. The full sequence is on the process page; comparing quotes shows what to check in anyone's bid. Visits and estimates are free.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Kissimmee & Greater Orlando crew based?

In Kissimmee, Florida. It's a service-area business with no storefront or street address, so the crew drives to your property. The Google Business Profile for this unit is set in Kissimmee, and the same crew covers Orange, Osceola, Seminole, Lake and Polk counties.

Do you work in Celebration, Poinciana, Lake Nona or Windermere?

Yes. Celebration and Poinciana are in Osceola County, Lake Nona and Windermere in Orange. Each has a page here with its own permit and HOA notes. If your community isn't listed, call (689) 354-0025 and ask.

Who pulls the permit in Osceola County versus Orange County?

We pull a permit when the work requires one. The offices differ: Osceola County issues a driveway permit with a 24-foot width limit for unincorporated lots, while unincorporated Orange County treats residential pavers as a zoning permit. A city address follows its own desk.

My HOA wants plans first. Can you help with that?

Yes. Associations like Baldwin Park, Laureate Park and Celebration each have their own review steps and deadlines. We can supply the dimensions, material and color the application asks for, and the approval comes from the association's board.

Is my paver driveway too far gone to just seal?

If the surface is level and only faded or stained, cleaning and sealing is the right call. If sections have sunk, rock underfoot or hold standing water, the base has moved, and restoration (lifting, re-compacting, relaying) comes before any sealer.

Does the Kissimmee crew also work on the Gulf coast?

No, that's the other crew. Sarasota and Manatee counties are handled by the Sarasota crew, which has its own phone line and knows that coast's salt air and water table.
